titulo: Do you have to let leftovers cool before putting them in the fridge?
fuentes: USDA FSIS — Leftovers and Food Safety: https://www.fsis.usda.gov/food-safety/safe-food-handling-and-preparation/food-safety-basics/leftovers-and-food-safety
USDA FSIS — Danger Zone (40–140 °F): bacteria can double in as little as 20 minutes
USDA FSIS: above 90 °F, no more than 1 hour out of the fridge
Origen del mito — iceboxes (Indiana Public Media, AARP Myth Buster)

frases.texto: You let your leftovers cool on the counter before they go in the fridge.
frases.estilo: Intrigue, like you're about to share a secret.
Dry and punchy, with a half smile.

frases.texto: On the counter, hot food can spend hours between forty and one hundred forty degrees.
In that zone, bacteria can double in as little as twenty minutes.
So where'd the myth come from?
Probably old iceboxes, where hot food melted the ice.
frases.estilo: Telling a friend, with a grin.

frases.texto: Today's fridges can handle it just fine.
Heads up: a giant pot takes forever to cool, even inside the fridge.
So split it into shallow containers.
The rule: in the fridge within two hours.
And if it's over ninety degrees out, one hour.
Send this to the friend who leaves the chili on the stove all night.
